text: A CloudWatch alarm watching one metric sounds simple, but four settings decide when it actually fires, one setting decides what it does when data goes missing, and a single-metric alarm on a borderline value tends to flap — firing and clearing over and over. Composite alarms are the real fix: instead of tuning one alarm's threshold until it's useless, you combine several alarms' states so only a genuinely corroborated problem pages anyone.

Statistic picks which aggregation you're evaluating — Average, Sum, Maximum, or a percentile like p99 — and period sets how long each data point covers. Evaluation periods and datapoints to alarm work together as an M-of-N rule: with 3 evaluation periods and 2 datapoints to alarm, the alarm fires only if at least 2 of the last 3 one-minute averages breached the threshold. One noisy minute alone won't trip it, but a real sustained spike will.

TreatMissingData decides what happens when a metric simply stops reporting — an instance scaling down, a Lambda that wasn't invoked. Left on its default, missing, that gap can leave a stale ALARM state in place even though nothing is actually wrong anymore. This is a genuinely common false-page cause: an alarm on a per-instance metric, left on default through a scale-in event, can fire purely because the instance and its metric no longer exist. Setting it explicitly to notBreaching, breaching, or ignore protects against exactly that.

A composite alarm doesn't watch a metric at all — it watches other alarms' states, combined with an AlarmRule using AND, OR, and NOT. ALARM on high p99 latency AND ALARM on elevated 5xx rate only trips when both are true together, so a latency blip alone, with error rates normal, no longer pages anyone. Adding AND NOT ALARM on deployment-in-progress suppresses the expected brief error blip during a planned rollout, without silencing real problems the rest of the time.

That's the real contrast: a single alarm on a borderline metric flips OK and ALARM back and forth, and every flip can notify someone. A composite alarm only enters ALARM when multiple underlying signals agree, which is a structural fix, not just a looser threshold. In practice, only the composite alarm needs an SNS topic or other action attached — the alarms it references can have their own notifications turned off entirely, so a human only ever hears from the composite.

Four settings define a standard alarm, TreatMissingData decides what a data gap means, and a composite alarm's AlarmRule is what actually stops flapping by requiring real corroboration.
